title: How many square bricks will cover the area?
description: An area of seven and a half square units is covered with square bricks whose side is one fifth of a unit. The area of one brick comes first, then the total area is divided by it using the reciprocal. Keeko doubts the working and thinks the area should be divided by the side of a brick.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of bricks is the total area divided by the area of one brick, and the area of a brick is side times side. Watch for students who divide by the side of the brick instead of its area.

source: Cover an area of 7 1/2 square units with square bricks each of whose sides is 1/5 unit. How many such square bricks are needed?
video_script.why: A learner sees that counting equal pieces is dividing the whole area by the area of one piece.
video_script.substitution: the book's own square bricks of side one fifth of a unit and the area of seven and a half square units
video_script.anchor: square bricks of side one fifth of a unit laid over an area of seven and a half square units
video_script.wrong_answer: thirty seven and a half bricks
video_script.wrong_move: divides the total area by the side of one brick, one fifth, instead of by its area
video_script.payoff_line: The bricks needed are three hundred seventy five halves.

final_answer.spoken: three hundred seventy five halves bricks

video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, one twenty fifth, fifteen halves, three hundred seventy five halves, seven and a half
maths_rules: area of one brick = 1/5 x 1/5 = (1 x 1)/(5 x 5) = 1/25 square unit
video_script.design: One square brick drawn with its side marked, then its area, then the whole area; the working band builds the division line by line.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a large area to be covered and one small square brick beside it

marks.brick: a small square brick appears with its side marked one fifth

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book, from one of the oldest geometry texts.
<bookmark mark='area'/>An area of seven and a half square units has to be covered with square bricks.
<bookmark mark='brick'/>The side of each brick is one fifth of a unit.
How many such bricks are needed?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside the area

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one square brick with its sides marked; a few bricks laid side by side inside the large area

marks.side: the side one fifth is marked on the brick
marks.area: the inside of the brick is shaded
marks.fill: bricks fill part of the large area

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>A square brick has four equal sides, and each side is one fifth of a unit.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The space inside the brick is its area, and a square brick has area side times side.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>The areas of all the bricks together must make the whole area.

beats.on_screen: Given: total area 7 1/2 square units; side of a brick 1/5 unit

marks.given: the area and the side are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the area to cover is seven and a half square units.
Each brick has a side of one fifth of a unit.

marks.find: the words number of bricks are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many bricks are needed.

beats.on_screen: area of a brick = side × side = 1/5 × 1/5 = (1 × 1) / (5 × 5) = 1/25 square unit

marks.sides: side times side is written with one fifth in both places
marks.mult: the numerators and the denominators are multiplied
marks.area: one twenty fifth square unit is boxed as the area of a brick

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step one, the area of a brick is its side times its side, one fifth times one fifth.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>One times one over five times five is one twenty fifth.
<bookmark mark='area'/>Each brick covers one twenty fifth of a square unit.

marks.mixed: seven and a half is written as a mixed number

narration: <bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step two, write the total area as a fraction, seven times two plus one over two.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>The total area is fifteen halves of a square unit.

beats.on_screen: number of bricks × 1/25 = 15/2, so number of bricks = 15/2 ÷ 1/25

marks.eq: the line number of bricks times area of a brick equals total area is written
marks.div: the division fifteen halves by one twenty fifth is written

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step three, the number of bricks times the area of one brick is the total area.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The number of bricks is fifteen halves divided by one twenty fifth.

marks.recip: twenty five is written as the reciprocal of one twenty fifth
marks.mult: twenty five is multiplied by fifteen halves

narration: <bookmark mark='recip'/>Step four, the reciprocal of the divisor, one twenty fifth, is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply the dividend by it, twenty five times fifteen over two.

marks.mixed: the mixed number is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The bricks needed are three hundred seventy five halves.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>That is one hundred eighty seven and a half bricks.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside one brick
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 15/2 ÷ 1/5 = 75/2 crossed out; the side of a brick and its area shown as different

marks.doubt: the working with one fifth appears
marks.diff: the side and the area of the brick light up in two colours
marks.fix: the working is crossed out and one twenty fifth returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks thirty seven and a half bricks are enough, after dividing by one fifth.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>But one fifth is the side of a brick, and not its area.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A brick covers an area, so we must divide by the area.
